slice: P2.4 unused MLINESTYLE removal with selected survivor offset edit
scope: Selected same-version AC1027 DXF, 2–255 contiguous 49/62/6 tuples, rooted dictionary, qualified original/survivor LTYPE providers and an original/live/output ordinary-MLINE census. The definition being changed is unused. Source and target ASCII/binary combinations are tested.

contract.operation: Remove original elements while retaining a nonempty ordered survivor list and changing retained offsets. ACI edits on different survivors can compose when each survivor has exactly one candidate across the union of its unchanged-offset and unchanged-ACI anchors and all remaining modeled fields.
contract.ambiguity: Full-tuple exact subsequence remains the first path. Otherwise all originals are searched once per survivor; the union must identify one unique original and preserve order. This cannot prove editing history or identify a survivor after both ACI and offset change unless it happens to match one original anchor. Competing raw changes, non-finite offsets, invalid resulting edited ACI, unqualified providers, missing/consumed ordinary MLINE evidence and late mutation refuse atomically.
contract.compatibilityRestriction: Compared with 5e2181d5, an ACI-only edit formerly admitted by an unchanged-offset anchor is now refused when its unchanged ACI and other fields also match another original through the offset-edit anchor. For A=(offset 1, ACI 1), B=(offset 2, ACI 2), a survivor (offset 1, ACI 2) is refused; sentinel and caller state remain intact, and correcting ACI to 3 succeeds using the same adapter. This narrowing avoids a cross-profile ambiguity. Existing full-tuple exact matching remains unchanged.
contract.bounds: The existing byte-sensitive work helper precharges the full source-string cross-product; the union compares common strings at most once per candidate. Typed/model copies remain separately bounded by retained bytes, not by a total CPU, RSS, allocator or concurrency cap.
contract.unqualified: Removed-to-zero edits, same-survivor changes without an independently matching anchor, linetype changes combined with removal, consumed-style geometry, unknown/proxy dependencies, earlier versions, native rendering and whole-document semantics remain open.

The final in-tree selector also covers this case.
